title: TOCSIN: a conflict-forecasting system with reference-class base rates and calibration scoring
description: A conflict-forecasting system whose every probability is a transparent reference-class base rate computed from the UCDP record: an explicit ladder (the unit's own history, its region, the world) conditioned on recency structure, with empirical-Bayes shrinkage and the class counts in view; a journal of operational questions with UCDP-pinned resolution criteria that grade themselves from each data refresh; and an arena that scores challenger forecasts (VIEWS, naive baselines, analyst overrides) against the engine on identical resolved outcomes. Evaluated walk-forward on the VIEWS target (7,680 country-months across five historical vantages), the system attains Brier 0.0461 against VIEWS's 0.0412 — within 12% of the state of the art — and five preregistered covariate families (regime type, horizon decay, youth bulges, militarized-dispute and alliance history, ethnic exclusion) all fail out-of-sample against the recency-conditioned base rates. The preprint in paper/ documents the transparency tax, an exact metric-blindness decomposition of the Brier score at rare-event base rates, and the equal-weight pool that beats every individual model. Code is MIT; the derived tables and registries are CC BY 4.0, built from UCDP/PRIO, Gleditsch–Ward, Correlates of War, EPR, V-Dem/OWID, Powell & Thyne, and World Bank sources — see DATA-RIGHTS.md for the layered attribution and required citations. The redistributable dataset bundle (tocsin-dataset-26.1, with full codebook) is attached to the GitHub release; the live deployment is at https://tocsin.karazajac.io.
